regime: Risk-on trend day. NQ and ES broke out together and closed near their highs above rising AVWAPs, powered by a 7.8% crude crash on Iran de-escalation and a strong ISM beat. Gold lagged and stayed below its stop; the only caution is how far and fast oil just repriced.
summary: Risk-on, clean and one-sided. NQ ripped 2.28% to close at 28,929, near its high and about 299 points above its 28,631 stop, with ES up 1.72% to a fresh 7,638 high and the Dow at a record. The fuel was oil: crude gapped down 7.81% over the weekend after Trump paused Iran strikes and OPEC+ lined up a September supply hike, which pulled yields lower and let the ISM beat (55.6 vs 54.0) do the rest. Every equity opening range broke up and price held above its AVWAP all session, a textbook trend day. Gold was the outlier, up a quiet 0.26% but still closed about 10 points under its stop, so its haven bid has not turned yet.
psychology: Trend days pay patience, not prediction. Today the tape showed its hand early: all four opening ranges broke the same way and price never gave back its AVWAP. The trap on a day like this is fading strength because it feels extended. Extended is not a signal. When price holds above a rising AVWAP and closes at the highs, the higher-probability play is with the trend on pullbacks, not against it on hope. Let the structure, not your gut, decide when the move is done.

event.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI (July) + Iran de-escalation
event.actual: ISM Manufacturing PMI 55.6, the highest since May 2022, with New Orders 56.7, Production 58.5, and Employment back in expansion at 52.8.
event.surprise: A clear beat, 55.6 versus 54.0. Layered on top: Trump paused Iran strikes and reopened diplomacy, and OPEC+ set a September output increase, both bearish for oil and risk-positive for equities.
event.nqReaction: NQ trended up all session to close +2.28% near its high; ES +1.72% to a new 7,638 high; the Dow printed a record. The de-escalation stripped a geopolitical premium out of oil and pulled yields down (10Y -1.68%), a clean risk-on combination for equities.

The Deviation Band edge is a fade tool for stretched, range-bound tape; today's one-directional trend is the wrong habitat for it.
